title: Vietnam conducts research on lab-grown meat

citation: Amirvaresi A., Ovissipour R. "Evaluation of Plant- and Microbial-Derived Protein Hydrolysates as Substitutes for Fetal Bovine Serum in Cultivated Seafood Cell Culture Media." bioRxiv preprint (2024).
title: Evaluation of Plant- and Microbial-Derived Protein Hydrolysates as Substitutes for Fetal Bovine Serum in Cultivated Seafood Cell Culture Media
author_or_publisher: Amirvaresi A., Ovissipour R. (Texas A&M University)
notes: Pea, mushroom, yeast, algae hydrolysates support zebrafish stem-cell growth only at 1 to 2.5% serum plus 0.01 mg/mL hydrolysate; serum-free alone cut membrane integrity. Abstract read.

citation: Stout A.J. et al. "A Beefy-R culture medium: Replacing albumin with rapeseed protein isolates." Biomaterials 296:122092 (2022).
title: A Beefy-R culture medium: Replacing albumin with rapeseed protein isolates
notes: Rapeseed protein isolate replaced recombinant albumin in Beefy-9, giving Beefy-R; bovine satellite cells grew over 4 passages with improved doubling time. Abstract read (Europe PMC).

citation: Schenzle L. et al. "Low-cost food-grade alternatives for serum albumins in FBS-free cell culture media." Scientific Reports 15:15296 (2025).
title: Low-cost food-grade alternatives for serum albumins in FBS-free cell culture media
notes: Food-grade stabilisers replaced recombinant albumin in B8/B9 medium; up to 73% medium-price reduction for some cell lines; transferable to porcine, chicken, CHO cells. Abstract read (Europe PMC).

citation: FAO and WHO. "Food safety aspects of cell-based food." Rome (2023).
title: Food safety aspects of cell-based food
notes: Hazard identification from a Nov 2022 Singapore expert consultation: 8 hazard categories across 4 production stages; most hazards known from conventional food; case studies Israel, Qatar, Singapore. Primary PDF returned HTTP 403; content via SLC-06 and search abstract, so Medium not High.

title: FAO and WHO consider the safety of cell-based food
notes: Summary of the FAO and WHO 2023 report: eight hazard categories (foreign matter, veterinary drugs, microbial toxins, additives, residues, allergens, microplastics, pathogens); four stages; most hazards familiar.
